subject: Request: Service guarantee tailoring and order form exhibit for RadiantHealth
messages:
From: Elena Moss <elena.moss@radianthealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@radianthealth.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Request: custom availability & latency exhibit for enterprise MSA

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. RadiantHealth is preparing the MSA and SOW for our pilot and procurement asked me to submit a formal request for a tailored SLA exhibit that includes both availability and a per-endpoint latency commitment for the imaging pipeline.

High level asks (we'll share the SOW once countersigned):
- Availability commitment for the inference endpoint used by our production imaging job: 99.95% per calendar month.
- P99 latency target for 2048-token inference calls: <= 220ms in us-west region.
- Operational runbook for failover to alternate region and estimated RTO/RPO.
- Evidence package for the past 90 days (uptime reports / latency percentiles) and any load-profile assumptions.

Attached is our standard procurement exhibit template and a short explanation of why we need the tighter latency bound (medical imaging inference in the loop with PACS). This is material to our internal approvers. Please confirm if Redwood can provide an addendum and proposed order form language. If there are material price or capacity implications we are open to discussing a dedicated capacity commitment.

Would appreciate a quick acknowledgement and an ETA for a first-draft exhibit.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Moss
Head of Procurement, RadiantHealth
elena.moss@radianthealth.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: RH_SLA_Addendum_Request_20270110.pdf (procurement exhibit template, 3 pages)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: custom availability & latency exhibit for RadiantHealth

Folks — forwarding RadiantHealth's request. TL;DR: they want 99.95% availability + P99 <=220ms for 2k tokens in us-west and runbook/evidence. Potentially willing to discuss dedicated capacity.

Quick thoughts / asks before I respond to Elena:
- Marissa: can you run a 90-day retrospective on our us-west fleet for the model they plan to use (see Deal RDW-ENT-3481) and pull P50/P95/P99 latencies for 512/1024/2048 token profiles? We need realistic language and an evidence pack.
- Ben: procurement may want dedicated pools; can you outline a starter dedicated-capacity offer and a delta to price (monthly commitment tiers)? Also flag whether the 220ms P99 for 2048 tokens is feasible without dedicated sizing.
- Legal/Procurement note: we'll need an availability exhibit and an availability exception if we can't meet 99.95 across multi-tenant. Propose offering a model-variant SLA: hosted 99.9% + latency best-effort, dedicated 99.95% + quantified latency SLO.

I'll draft an initial exhibit doc and send to Elena by Wednesday EOD. If either of you sees blockers please shout.

-Karthik

Attachment: redwood-proposed-availability-exhibit_v1.docx (draft, not customer-facing)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: custom availability & latency exhibit for RadiantHealth

Karthik — ran the retrospective. Key findings (us-west, last 90 days) for the candidate model: 
- 512 tokens: P50 48ms, P95 82ms, P99 130ms
- 1024 tokens: P50 86ms, P95 140ms, P99 210ms
- 2048 tokens: P50 165ms, P95 290ms, P99 420ms

Notes: the 2048-token P99 at scale spikes when we hit concurrent-burst windows and during rolling kernel updates. With current multi-tenant routing we see occasional tails to 400-500ms. We could get closer to 220ms P99 for 2048 tokens with a combination of: dedicated GPU pool, reserved throughput (soft reservations), and KV-prefix caching for repeated imaging prompts. That will require capacity commitments.

I've uploaded a short evidence pack (latency-percentiles.csv, uptime-summary.pdf) to the deal Drive link and attached a customer-ready exhibit that frames options: hosted availability 99.9% with latency best-effort; dedicated pool availability 99.95% + latency SLOs per token-band.

Marissa

Attachment: latency-percentiles.csv, uptime-summary.pdf, RH_exhibit_customer_v1.docx

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: custom availability & latency exhibit for RadiantHealth

Karthik / Marissa — quick capacity & pricing note. To achieve P99 <=220ms for sustained 2048-token mixes we recommend the following starter configuration:
- Dedicated pod: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (or q4-quantized inference rigs) with pinned model shards
- Baseline reservations: 250 reqs/sec sustained, burst to 750 reqs/sec (autoscale with warm standby)
- One-time onboarding & validation: $35k
- Monthly reserved fee: $85k (covers nodes + 24/7 support & runbook)
- SLA uplift: +0.5% availability commitment; if they move to this configuration we can commit to 99.95% and advertise measured P99 latency SLO with quarterly evidence reports.

If RadiantHealth wants lower latency tail guarantees we can tighten with a higher reservation. I'll prepare a short order-form exhibit with pricing options.

Ben

Attachment: dedicated-config-options.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Moss <elena.moss@radianthealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Service guarantee tailoring and order form exhibit for RadiantHealth

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Apologies for the short delay while we pulled data and scoped options. Summary and next steps below.

Summary of what we can offer today (two tracks):

1) Hosted (multi-tenant) option — pilot-friendly
- Availability: 99.9% per calendar month
- Latency: best-effort (we will provide P50/P95/P99 reports monthly)
- Evidence: 90-day retrospective attached + ongoing monthly percentile reports
- Order form implication: no upfront capacity commitment; standard per-token pricing applies

2) Dedicated capacity option — enterprise SLA and latency SLOs
- Availability: 99.95% per calendar month (availability exhibit)
- Latency SLO: P99 <=220ms for 2048-token requests in us-west under the agreed baseline reservation
- Baseline reservation: 250 reqs/sec sustained; burst policy and autoscale to 750 reqs/sec (detailed in order form)
- Pricing: onboarding $35k; monthly reserved fee starting $85k (see attached options)
- Evidence & ops: quarterly latency audits, runbook for regional failover, and a 24/7 escalation contact

Attachments: I have attached a customer-facing availability exhibit (RH_exhibit_customer_v1.docx) and a draft order form section that codifies the reservation and pricing. We'll also share the 90-day evidence bundle via the Drive link above.

Ask for RadiantHealth:
- Please confirm which track you prefer (hosted pilot vs dedicated reserve) and whether the reservation sizing matches your anticipated workload.
- If you want the dedicated route, procurement can sign the order form addendum and we will schedule a capacity validation and onboarding window (2–4 weeks typical).
- If you have amendments to the exhibit language, please mark up the attached doc and return — Marissa and I will iterate quickly.

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call next week to walk the exhibit and order form with your engineering & procurement teams.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0112

Attachments: RH_exhibit_customer_v1.docx, dedicated-config-options.xlsx, latency-percentiles.csv
